# FDG3076

> DO name event argument classes with the “EventArgs” suffix, as shown in the following example:

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 3.6.3 Names of Events.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1710
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

CA1710 reports a class derived from System.EventArgs, directly or through another class such as CancelEventArgs, whose name does not end with EventArgs. It checks the whole hierarchy because the package sets dotnet_code_quality.CA1710.exclude_indirect_base_types = false (see FDG3048; probe with SDK 10.0.403). On the noise samples the option added 2 CA1710 reports, both true and neither for this suffix (docs/noise-samples.md). Renaming a public type changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; CA1710 has no code fix.

## From the book

```csharp
public class ClickedEventArgs : EventArgs {
  int x;
  int y;
  public ClickedEventArgs (int x, int y) {
     this.x = x;
     this.y = y;
  }
  public int X { get { return x; } }
  public int Y { get { return y; } }
}
```
